name: compose-agent
description: An agent profile assembled from lower layers: what it is good at and not for, a model class that names a routing prefix and never a vendor, a declared tool surface, input and output shapes, a cost class and a max-concurrency ceiling, run as one isolated turn with the grading criterion absent from everything the unit can read. Load it when declaring a new agent profile or its good_at/not_for pair, when deciding which tools or packaged skills an agent unit may reach, when sequencing which profile handles which workflow step, when a running agent needs to delegate to a sub-agent with its own identity-chain hop and a budget slice cut from the parent, when checking whether a criterion could leak into an agent's context, or when reasoning about keeping well over a hundred concurrently running agents coherent.

purpose.text: Assemble a bounded loop, a declared tool surface and a packaged capability set into one agent unit that runs isolated, declared up front by what it is good at so a caller knows how to call it and how to sequence it.
purpose.quote: Each agent is defined up front by what it is good at, so callers know how to call it and how to sequence it.

operations.name: declare_agent (proposed operation set; a composition introduces no new interface, so these are assembly points over interfaces the lower layers already publish)
operations.input: a profile - good_at, not_for, model_class, the declared tools[], input/output shapes, cost_class, max_concurrency - plus the budget and depth already consumed by whatever is calling it (proposed)
operations.output: a priced admission plan whose cost is one turn under the declared model_class and cost_class, or a refusal issued before anything runs when a declared tool or capability cannot be resolved (proposed)

operations.name: admit_agent (proposed)
operations.output: one isolated unit bound to exactly the declared tool surface and exactly the declared capability set, with nothing else reachable from inside it (proposed)

operations.name: invoke_turn (proposed)
operations.input: the admitted unit's session handle and one task built from input_from, carrying the declared input fields and never the criterion (proposed)
operations.output: one turn result - stop reason, outputs, usage - reconciled against the admission plan's cost (proposed)

operations.name: delegate (proposed)
operations.input: a sub-agent profile name, a task, the parent's delegation chain, and a budget slice cut from the parent's remaining ceiling (proposed)
operations.output: the sub-agent's turn result plus one new chain hop recorded against it, so the sub-agent's spend and its actor both trace back to the same root as the parent's (proposed)

operations.name: release_agent (proposed)
operations.input: the unit and its turn result (proposed)
operations.output: the unit terminated, its cost reconciled up the tree, and one record naming which of the profile's declared outputs were produced (proposed)

shapes.name: agent-profile (proposed summary shape, field names kept identical to examples/end-to-end/schemas/agent-profile.schema.json and examples/end-to-end/agents.json; the full schema, the delegation-call shape and three worked declarations are in references/usage.md)
shapes.quote: Each agent is defined up front by what it is good at, so callers know how to call it and how to sequence it.

schema.title: AgentProfile
schema.description: Proposed. Declared once, before any unit is admitted. model_class is a routing prefix, never a vendor.

not_for.description: The call that should go to a different profile.

model_class.description: A routing class by prefix, never a vendor.

tools.description: Exactly what admit_agent binds. Nothing else is reachable.

inputs.description: required[] and fields{}; see references/usage.md for the full shape.

outputs.description: required[] and fields{}; see references/usage.md for the full shape.

shapes.name: agent-admission (proposed shape: what declare_agent resolves a profile to before any unit is admitted)

declared_tools.description: Bound at admission; admit_agent asserts the unit's actual tool list equals this exactly.

capability_set.description: The packaged skills this unit may load; nothing undeclared may load.

cost_ceiling_micros.description: This unit's slice of whatever ceiling called it.

correlation.description: Inherited, never re-derived: run_id, correlation_id, depth.

shapes.name: delegation-call (proposed shape: what a running agent hands a sub-agent, an internal step rather than a fresh entry - REF-3-4-15's rule, which compose-loop already applies to a loop's own root and this shape applies to a delegate call; field names for the chain follow examples/end-to-end/schemas/entry.schema.json's actor.delegation_chain)

schema.title: DelegationCall
schema.description: Proposed. Not an entry envelope: it reports into a run that already exists rather than minting one.

delegation_chain.description: The parent's chain plus exactly one new hop for the sub-agent.

budget_slice_micros.description: Cut from the parent's remaining ceiling, never a fresh root ceiling.

shapes.name: What a refusal looks like (proposed worked instance): an agent step asks for a tool outside its declared list

schema.title: Refused before the unit could reach a tool it never declared
schema.description: The registered policy-denied row in docs/decomposition.md section 2.1.6: a scope refusal is a policy refusal, and it carries rule_id.

examples.title: Tool outside the unit's declared tool surface
examples.detail: unit code-fixer-0007 requested run_shell, which is not in its declared tools [read_file, write_file, run_tests]

invariants.text: The profile is declared up front by what it is good at, and TARGET T6.5 states the reason: a caller has to be able to name what an agent is good at and how to sequence it before it is ever called. What compose-agent adds is the fixed field set that makes that declaration checkable rather than a paragraph of prose: good_at, not_for, model_class, tools, input/output shapes, cost_class and max_concurrency, matching examples/end-to-end/schemas/agent-profile.schema.json's required list.
invariants.quote: Each agent is defined up front by what it is good at, so callers know how to call it and how to sequence it.

invariants.text: cap-agent-runtime already states that one prompt turn with a stop reason is the unit an agent runs (F-b3-05). What this composition adds: admission happens once per unit, before the turn opens - the tool surface and the capability set are bound at admit_agent, not renegotiated call by call inside the turn.
invariants.quote: The middle column is the contract

invariants.text: cap-isolation already states that a unit of work runs isolated (F-b3-02). What compose-agent adds: an agent is exactly one isolation admission, so nothing about a concurrently running sibling agent - its inputs, its partial outputs, its own admission - is reachable from inside this one. That containment, repeated per unit, is what keeps TARGET T6.6's well-over-a-hundred concurrent agents coherent without a shared coordinator watching all of them at once.
invariants.quote: The target scale is well over a hundred agents running at a time, working together, managing state, breaking problems down, and self-improving where they can.

invariants.text: Proposed: cap-tool-access already states the operations an agent's declared tools are bound through (F-b3-06); cap-capability-packaging already states the operations its declared capability set is resolved through (F-b3-07). What compose-agent adds is the exactness: the tool list a unit actually holds after admit_agent equals the profile's declared tools[] exactly, and the skills it can load equal its declared capability set exactly - the two assertions decomposition.md section 3.5 row M4 names alongside the criterion's absence.

Proposed: models are reached only through cap-model-access, and a profile's model_class is a routing class rather than a vendor - the same rule agentic-stack already states for every caller (F-a4-01). A profile that named a vendor model would make the swap agentic-stack requires of that capability impossible to honour from this layer.

agentic-stack already states design rule 6, that the grader is never visible to the graded (F-b1-07, F-b2-05). What compose-agent adds: core-judge grades a turn's result against criterion_ref after invoke_turn returns, never before, and the task built for invoke_turn is assembled from input_from and the declared input fields only - there is no field in the turn-request shape a wrapper at this layer could use to smuggle the criterion back in.
invariants.quote: An agent sees its outcome, never the criterion it is judged against

invariants.text: Proposed, drawing on xc-identity-delegation (F-b4-03) and xc-budget (F-b4-02, F-b1-08): a delegate call adds exactly one hop to the chain the parent already carries and cuts a slice from the ceiling the parent already has, never a fresh root actor and never a fresh root ceiling. A hundred agents delegating in parallel therefore still sum to one traceable chain and one traceable ceiling apiece, rather than a hundred untraceable ones.

Proposed: compose-loop already states that a loop's iterations sum upward and that depth is bounded and checked at resolve time, not run time. What compose-agent adds: an agent invoked from a loop body is one more kind that must declare its cost contribution in that iteration's envelope - a fix-and-check loop whose body is an agent step is not a special case, it nests exactly the way any other step nests.
invariants.quote: Depth must be bounded, and checked at resolve time, not run time.

invariants.text: Proposed: compose-loop already states that stop and cap are opposite terminations that must not be collapsed (REF-5-3-08). What compose-agent adds: a unit that ran out of its budget slice mid-turn is a cap, never a quiet success, however useful its partial output - the same distinction a loop's iteration ceiling makes, applied to one agent's turn.
invariants.quote: opposites and must not be collapsed

invariants.text: Reach the agent the way any capability is reached: TARGET T6.2's four entries - a human, an event, a schedule, an external system or agent - all name the same workflow_ref and the same agent step, and none of them may mint a fresh root agent invocation from inside a running turn. Proposed, following the reference example: a running unit's result may steer a later step; it may not start a new one with no actor and no ceiling of its own.
invariants.quote: Four entries cover nearly every situation: a human, an event, a schedule (time), and an external system or agent. All four enter through the same shape.

not_exposed.text: compose-loop already states, citing design rule 6 (F-b1-07), that the grader is never visible to the graded. compose-agent's consequence: the criterion string, the checks sampled for a grading, and the criterion-set digest never enter the task built for invoke_turn, the unit's environment, or anything the profile's declared inputs could carry - decomposition.md section 3.5 row M4 states this as the composition-level assertion that the criterion is absent from everything the unit can read.
not_exposed.quote: The grader is never visible to the graded.

not_exposed.text: Which product serves the runtime, the isolation boundary, the tool endpoint or the packaging store behind any one profile. agentic-stack already states that products belong in the adapter column only (F-part-c-09); an agent profile carries a model_class prefix and a tool name, never a vendor or a version.
not_exposed.quote: Products belong in the adapter column only

not_exposed.text: Proposed: another concurrently admitted agent's unit_id, its inputs, its partial outputs or its own cost ceiling. Nothing a sibling unit is doing is a field this composition exposes to the unit in hand, which is the isolation boundary restated as a fact about the composition rather than about the sandbox alone.

instructions.action: Declare the profile before admitting anything: good_at entries specific enough to route on, not_for, model_class as a routing prefix, the declared tools[], input/output shapes, cost_class and max_concurrency. Resolve it with declare_agent to a priced admission plan before any unit runs.
instructions.why: TARGET T6.5 is the reason the fields exist at all: a caller has to be able to tell what an agent is good at and how to sequence it without opening the agent itself.
instructions.quote: so callers know how to call it and how to sequence it

instructions.action: Proposed: admit the unit through cap-isolation, bind its tool surface through cap-tool-access to exactly the declared tools[], and resolve its capability set through cap-capability-packaging to exactly the declared package list, once, at admission, before the first turn opens. Check design rule 6 again at this same boundary, per this skill's definition of done: assert the criterion string is absent from everything the unit can read, the unit's bound tool list equals the declared tools[] exactly, and no undeclared skill loaded.
instructions.why: Proposed: cap-isolation, cap-tool-access and cap-capability-packaging each already own the operation that does this; what a composition adds is doing all three together, once, so nothing not named in the profile is reachable from inside the unit - and decomposition.md section 3.5 row M4 names the same three assertions as what makes that binding checkable rather than assumed.

instructions.action: Reach the model only through cap-model-access, addressed by the profile's model_class prefix. Never let a profile, a task, or an admission record name a vendor or a specific model.
instructions.why: agentic-stack already states that callers request a class, never a vendor, and that the prefix carries the contract; a profile is exactly such a caller.
instructions.quote: Callers request a class, never a vendor.

instructions.action: Run the unit's work as one prompt turn through cap-agent-runtime's invoke_turn, per the Agent Client Protocol that capability names: build the task from input_from and the declared input fields only, take back the stop reason, the outputs and the usage, and reconcile the cost against the admission plan.
instructions.why: cap-agent-runtime already fixes the turn as the unit of agent execution; a composition adds nothing to that shape, it only supplies the task and reads the result.

instructions.action: Hand the turn's result to core-judge for a verdict against criterion_ref; never let the agent, the profile, or the task carry the criterion itself.
instructions.why: agentic-stack states design rule 6 as a test, and compose-loop already applies it to a loop's own exit condition (F-b1-07, F-b2-05): does the grading criterion ever travel with the thing graded. An agent composition is exactly where a well-meaning wrapper could add it back in by accident, so the rule has to be checked again here.

instructions.action: When one agent delegates to another, call delegate: append exactly one hop to the delegation chain already carried by the run, and cut the sub-agent's budget from the remaining slice rather than opening a fresh root ceiling. Terminate the unit and reconcile its cost up the tree on every stop reason, not only on end_turn - including a delegated sub-agent's return - and report a unit that used its full budget slice as a cap, never as a quiet success, whatever it produced.
instructions.why: Proposed, drawing on xc-identity-delegation and xc-budget: every action names an actor and every unit of work carries a ceiling, so a delegation that skipped either would be an actor with no chain or a spend with no ceiling above it; following the reference example, stop and cap are opposite terminations, and collapsing them at the same reconciliation point is a mistake the reference records as already made once.

instructions.action: When the agent's work is iterative, put the agent step inside compose-loop's body instead of writing a private retry inside the agent. Let the loop's per-iteration ceiling, its depth bound checked at resolve time, and its three-way termination apply to the agent step exactly as they apply to any other step.
instructions.why: Proposed, following the reference example: a nested plan lies about cost unless costs sum upward, and depth has to be bounded and checked before anything executes rather than discovered two iterations in.

instructions.action: compose-loop already states, citing TARGET T6.3 and T6.2, that any entry can call complex workflows, agents and loops that run across the entire stack. Reach the agent the same way: one entry envelope, whichever of the four entries you are, naming the workflow and the agent step the intent points at, and never mint a fresh root agent invocation from inside a running turn.
instructions.why: Any entry can call complex workflows, agents and loops that run across the entire stack, so an agent's size and its concurrency belong to the composition, not to which door the call came through.
instructions.quote: Any entry can call complex workflows, agents, and loops that run across the entire stack.

instructions.action: Set max_concurrency from what the isolation adapter can actually admit at once, not from a round number. Treat well over a hundred agents running concurrently as an ordinary point on that scale: each unit's own isolation boundary, its own budget slice and its own chain hop are what keep that many runs coherent, not a coordinator that watches all of them.
instructions.why: TARGET T6.6 states the target scale directly; the mechanism this skill can offer for reaching it without a central bottleneck is the containment, budget and identity guarantees already declared per unit.
instructions.quote: working together, managing state, breaking problems down, and self-improving where they can

instructions.action: Proposed: open references/usage.md for the full agent-profile schema, the delegation-call shape, a worked declaration for each of TARGET T1's three ways in, and the worked rejection in full. The body of this skill is enough to declare a conformant agent without it.
instructions.why: Proposed: the full schema and three worked declarations would push this skill past its instruction and shape budget without adding anything the body does not already state.

best_practices.text: agentic-stack already states that callers request a class, never a vendor (F-a4-01). What it adds here: model_class is a required field of the profile itself, so the composer never has an opportunity to fill in a vendor at this layer either - there is no field left over to put one in.

cap-agent-runtime already states that a stop reason is not a verdict (F-a7-03). What compose-agent adds for a caller sequencing agents: end_turn means this unit stopped, not that its output is acceptable to whatever step reads it next - ask core-judge, and never substitute a stop reason for a verdict when deciding whether to continue a workflow.

Proposed: write good_at entries specific enough to route on. A router takes input, determines intent, and routes the request to a handler without knowing what the handler does; the records on file describe this as the reason a router pattern scales, and it only works if good_at is a claim precise enough to route against rather than a category. The record is a search result rather than a page read, so take the shape and not a measurement from it.
best_practices.quote: A router takes input, determines intent, and routes the request to a handler without knowing what the handler does.

best_practices.text: Proposed: treat a delegation call as an ordinary outcome of a turn, not a failure to have routed correctly the first time. The records on file describe a handoff as an agent explicitly saying another profile is better equipped to continue, which is the same shape as this composition's delegate operation; the record is a search result rather than a page read.
best_practices.quote: this other agent is better equipped to handle this entire conversation from here on

best_practices.text: Proposed: keep the profile declaration itself independent of which runtime, registry or process happens to serve it. The records on file describe an agent registry as a control plane that does not care how an agent runs, only that it is registered, governed and observable; that is the property this skill's own second adapter exists to test. The record is a search result rather than a page read.
best_practices.quote: does not care how your agent runs, only that it is registered, governed, and observable

best_practices.text: Proposed: pick max_concurrency from a measured admission ceiling, not from an aspiration. A number the isolation adapter cannot actually honour concurrently is not a max, it is a promise the platform breaks the first time a hundred callers test it at once.

adapters.maps_to: declare_agent, admit_agent and invoke_turn served by resolving a profile name against a JSON file held in the same process as the composer, admitting the unit through cap-isolation and calling cap-agent-runtime directly. examples/end-to-end/agents.json declares seven profiles; examples/end-to-end/schemas/agent-profile.schema.json is the schema every one of them satisfies, requiring name, good_at, not_for, model_class, tools, inputs, outputs, cost_class and max_concurrency; examples/end-to-end/run.py resolves an agent step's profile field against that file and dispatches it through one dispatch interface in the same walk that runs every other operator. Proposed entity id: the knowledge base has no capability row for agent composition, so there is no E- record to reuse and this id is ours.
adapters.cannot: Cannot discover a profile published outside this process or repository, cannot answer 'what agents exist' to a caller that only speaks a network protocol, and cannot authenticate a remote party against anything other than the identity chain this same process already trusts; the registry is a lookup table read at composer start, not a service another party can query.
adapters.swap_procedure: Point declare_agent at a remote registry entry instead of a row in agents.json, admit the returned profile the same way, and run one conformance report over both. agentic-stack states design rule 3 - every interface ships with at least two adapters, and the second exists to prove the first is not load-bearing - and this pair is that test applied to a profile registry.
adapters.quote: Each agent is defined up front by what it is good at, so callers know how to call it and how to sequence it.

adapters.maps_to: the same declare_agent and admit_agent served by a remote agent protocol server: a profile is a signed, network-addressable registry entry rather than a row in a file the composer already has open, and admitting a unit means authenticating to that server and receiving a session over the network instead of instantiating a process in the same container. Proposed entity id: no swap-candidate entity exists in the knowledge base for this shape either, so it is minted the same way this skill's first adapter is.
adapters.cannot: Cannot resolve a profile without a network round trip, so declare_agent fails for reasons an in-process registry never can - the server is unreachable, the entry's signature does not verify; and cannot assume its identity chain and the composer's are issued by the same authority, so the hop it adds must be a token exchange rather than a direct hop.
adapters.swap_procedure: Publish one profile to both the in-process file and a conformant remote registry, run declare_agent against each for the same task, and assert adapters_run >= 2 with identical required admission fields - good_at, model_class, tools, cost_class, max_concurrency - even though the network round trip and the identity hop differ.
adapters.quote: Every action names an actor, including delegated agent actors. Delegation chains are explicit

definition_of_done.criterion: Proposed tool: `python3 tools/agent_conformance.py --profiles examples/end-to-end/agents.json --units 20 --report out/agent-conformance.json`. For each of 20 admitted units it mounts a sentinel criterion string into the run's working state the way core-judge's criterion_ref would resolve it, runs the unit's declared task, and asserts: the sentinel string is absent from everything the unit can read (files, environment, tool list, prompt) so criterion_leaks stays 0; the unit's bound tool list equals agents.json's declared tools[] for that profile exactly so tool_mismatches stays 0; and the set of capabilities the unit actually loaded equals its declared capability set exactly so undeclared_skills stays 0. Assert units_checked == 20.
definition_of_done.expected: agent-conformance: units_checked=20, criterion_leaks=0, tool_mismatches=0, undeclared_skills=0; exit 0
definition_of_done.breakage: Mount the criterion file into the unit's filesystem alongside its declared inputs, the way decomposition.md section 3.5 row M4 states as the deliberate breakage for this row.
definition_of_done.expected_failure: criterion_leaks becomes non-zero for every unit whose working directory includes the mounted file: `FAIL: unit code-fixer-0007 read criterion sentinel at /work/.criterion`, criterion_leaks=20, while tool_mismatches and undeclared_skills stay 0 on the same run - isolating the fault to design rule 6 rather than to the tool or packaging binding. Status claimed: tools/agent_conformance.py does not exist in this repository yet, so neither run has been executed.
definition_of_done.quote: The grader is never visible to the graded.

open_questions.question: Should compose-agent build on cap-model-access, core-judge, xc-identity-delegation and xc-budget? Its contract fixes model_class routing through cap-model-access, grading through core-judge, and delegation through an identity chain and a subdivided budget, but docs/skill-manifest.json lists none of the four under this skill's builds_on, so those rows are stated here with no link to the skill that owns each fact. Reported, not edited: composes_with equals the manifest exactly.
open_questions.evidence: A manifest revision adding the links, or a decision that a composition may cite a capability or cross-cutting concern it does not build on, the same question compose-loop already raised for cap-durable-execution.
open_questions.default: Name each capability and its kb ids in the rows that need it, and leave builds_on as the manifest has it.

open_questions.question: Is a max_concurrency chosen per profile enough to keep TARGET T6.6's well-over-a-hundred concurrent agents coherent, or does coherence at that scale need a resource beyond what any one capability in this skill's builds_on states - a scheduler that admits across profiles rather than within one?
open_questions.evidence: A load test running many profiles concurrently against a shared isolation adapter, recording whether per-profile max_concurrency values are jointly honoured or whether the adapter's own admission ceiling is crossed first.
open_questions.default: Treat max_concurrency as a per-profile ceiling only, and rely on cap-isolation's own admission limit as the platform-wide backstop, revisiting if a load test finds the two disagree.
open_questions.quote: well over a hundred agents running at a time

open_questions.question: The knowledge base has no capability row for agent composition, so which entities should today's adapter and its second be recorded against?
open_questions.evidence: 1-3-1 applied (TARGET T5): the three options were to record today's adapter against an existing capability entity such as agent runtime, to mint new entities for the composition layer, or to leave the adapters[] pair absent. Recording against agent runtime would misattribute an in-process registry's own row to a different B3 line (the citation defect a prior ceremony already named); leaving the pair absent would leave the round's explicit instruction to cite examples/end-to-end unaddressed. Recommendation taken: mint both, the way compose-operators already did for the operator layer, and say so in each row.
open_questions.default: Both adapters[].entity ids are recorded as proposed and pending a knowledge-base entity if PASS.md ever grows a composition-layer row.
